Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Top Story Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings protests ‘disrespect’ at COP31 as summit president apologises Source : Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen I engrwinaamzua@gmail.com 22 November 2026 6:04pm COP31 President Murat Kurum and Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings in a pose after smoking the peace pipe. ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ghana’s Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has protested what she described as disrespectful treatment at the closing plenary of COP31 after she was interrupted while delivering the African Group’s position on the final climate decision.
COP31 President Murat Kurum subsequently apologised to the Minister and the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) following objections from the Ghanaian delegation.
Dr Agyeman-Rawlings, who was speaking on behalf of the African Group, expressed disappointment that another delegate had been allowed to deliver an intervention without interruption, while she was cut off during her address.
“I wish to express my profound disappointment that, while another Party was delivering its intervention on the COP cover decision, that delegate was allowed to speak without interruption. However, I was rudely interrupted and cut off while delivering my statement by Your Excellency,” she said.
She described the incident as an example of the treatment the African Group had endured throughout the negotiations and registered the bloc’s strongest objection.
“This, Mr President, is an example of the level of disrespect we have endured and against which we continue to register our strongest objection,” she said.
Dr Agyeman-Rawlings, daughter of Ghana's late President, Jerry John Rawlings, argued that the incident was inconsistent with the principles of multilateralism, transparency and fairness underpinning the Paris Agreement.
She also disclosed that she had changed her flight arrangements twice and extended her stay by several days to fulfil her responsibilities and participate fully in the negotiations.
The Minister subsequently called for an opportunity to deliver her statement before the adoption of the final COP decision.
In response to the protest, Mr Kurum acknowledged the concerns and apologised to Dr Agyeman-Rawlings and the African Group of Negotiators.
He said he had not intended to disrespect Ghana, the Minister or the wider African negotiating bloc.
Beyond the interruption, Dr Agyeman-Rawlings outlined the African Group’s reservations about the final climate decision, saying it fell short of the best possible outcome for the continent.
Among the concerns raised was the decision’s reaffirmation of the goal of at least tripling adaptation finance by 2035.
The incident came as African countries sought to push for stronger commitments on climate finance and support for vulnerable nations in the outcome of the negotiations.
